newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia refinances $150 million syndicated loan.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia refinances $150 million syndicated loan.

text.p: Tunisia has signed for a $150 million syndicated bank loan, banking and finance officials said on Tuesday.
The loan is for a seven-year term with a five-year grace period, they said.
The deal was priced at Libor+0.5 for the first five years and Libor+0.6 for the two last years.
The convention was signed with a group of 24 banks by Finance Minister Nouri Zorgati on Monday in Paris for the Republic of Tunisia.
This is the second syndicated loan Tunisia has signed this year. In January, it refinanced a $222 million syndicated loan, a five year transaction priced at 70 basis points over LIBOR.
Last week, Tunisia's Central Bank said that 15 billion yen worth of 4.95 percent 15-year Samurai bonds was fully subscribed in less than a week in Tokyo.
Officials said the total resources Tunisia tapped on the international capital markets to finance the state's budget deficit has so far reached $500 million.
Tunisia's last rating was BBB+ by JBRI.
The banks who arranged the refinancing are: London-based Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi limited, Dresdner Bank Luxembourg SA, Natwest, Societe Generale, and ABD International Bank.
